paper_summary: Analytical paper proposing a closed-form model for the thermal conductivity of syntactic foams with spherical microballoons: the hollow microballoon is first replaced by an equivalent homogeneous filler (Benveniste-Miloh), then the composite conductivity is derived with an Eshelby model modified by the Mori-Tanaka mean-field approach. The model system is polypropylene filled with hollow silicate microballoons TK35 (35 um OD, 680 kg/m3) and TK70 (70 um OD, 210 kg/m3) at microballoon volume fractions up to 0.25, with constituent data taken from Liang & Li (Polym. Test. 2006, 2007). Predictions agree well with the literature experiments and lie between the experimental and 3D FEA results; parametric studies show the foam conductivity rises with relative wall thickness and volume fraction, strongly so for high shell/matrix conductivity ratio.

extraction_notes: The paper reports NO numerical composite (PP + microballoon) property values: predicted, experimental and 3D-FEA conductivities appear only as normalized curves keff/km vs fmb in Fig. 2 (fmb = 0-0.25) and as parametric curves in Fig. 3, so composite records at specific microballoon volume fractions could not be created (reading values off plots is not permitted, and reproducing them by evaluating eq. (22) myself would be generating rather than extracting numbers). The three records above cover every number the paper does state numerically, all from Table 1 and Sec. 3: (1) the unfilled PP matrix conductivity 0.235 W/mK (secondary - Table 1 constituent data cited to Liang & Li, refs 16,17); (2)-(3) the model-computed effective conductivities of the TK35 and TK70 hollow microballoons themselves, 0.06035 and 0.03364 W/mK (data_origin 'model', eq. (6)). For records 2 and 3 the hollow particle is encoded as its own two-phase system: matrix_class = 'other' is the silicate shell (2210 kg/m3, k = 0.17934 W/mK) and particle_volume_fraction is the enclosed gas core volume fraction fc (0.692 / 0.905, stated in the text), NOT a microballoon loading in a foam. particle_wall_thickness_ratio eta = inner/outer radius was obtained from the stated inner and outer diameters (30.963/35 = 0.885; 67.710/70 = 0.967) and is consistent with the stated fc = eta^3. Unit conversions: densities kg/m3 -> g/cm3 (680 -> 0.68, 210 -> 0.21); Table 1 labels the diameters 'mm' but they are micrometres (text: 'the average diameters of the microballoons, TK35 and TK70, are 35 and 70 mm'). Experimental composite conductivity data for these systems must be sourced from the original papers, Liang & Li, Polym. Test. 25 (2006) 527-531 and 26 (2007) 419-424.
